title: Semantic anchor replay and cohort resilience runner
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: We need a lightweight, CI-friendly mechanism to replay a curated set of semantic anchor prompts across model rollouts and cohort slices to detect subtle regressions that generic smoke tests miss. Motivation: existing smoke suites catch gross regressions but miss drift tied to semantic anchors (e.g., domain-specific phrasings) and cohort-based instability. This PR introduces a standalone 'runner' that schedules controlled replays, computes a resilience score per cohort, and surfaces actionable signals to CI and the eval dashboard.

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a scheduling runner (eval/runner/) that replays a canonical semantic-anchor prompt set against a matrix of model versions and cohort definitions with configurable concurrency and backoff.
- Implements a resilience metric that combines anchor fidelity (semantic similarity + ranked output stability) and temporal variance into a single score.
- Integrates with CI as a gated advisory: low-severity regressions add a softfail label and file a Linear task; high-severity regressions can fail the CI gate (configurable by repo/team).
- Provides a compact reporter JSON and a permalinkable dashboard summary hook (for Redwood Console ingestion).
- Adds unit + integration tests and a lightweight mock backend used by CI to avoid flakiness.

Checklist:
- [x] Runner core + scheduler implemented
- [x] Resilience scorer + explainability fields added
- [x] CI adapter + gating policy (softfail/hardfail) added
- [x] Tests for core logic and CI path
- [x] Docs: developer guide + example config

Why this design: The runner is intentionally pluggable and conservative: replays are budgeted, and we use a two-stage gating (soft advisory -> escalated fail) to avoid noisy CI breakage. The resilience score is designed for quick triage (0-100) and includes a minimal explainability payload (top anchor diffs and a dominant token-change signature).

Notes on usage: teams can opt-in to hard fail by adding a policy entry under .eval/config/replay-policies.yaml. Default is team-level softfail with auto-Linear-ticket creation for severity >= 60.

Related: ENG-2021, ENG-2145.

review_conversation:
Jordan Li (reviewer): Can you clarify how the runner avoids causing flakiness in CI?
Maya Chen (author): The runner defaults to softfail and uses the mock backend in CI to avoid external LLM variability; we also debounce alerts with a sliding window (configurable). See eval/runner/config.yaml.example for backoff settings.
Diego Ramirez (reviewer): The resilience score aggregation feels opaque — can you add a short doc or inline comments explaining the weights?
Maya Chen: Added doc section and inline comments in scorer.py and included a simple worked example in eval/docs/replay-runner.md.
Ava Singh (reviewer): Any privacy implications for sending prompt anchors to the reporter hook?
Maya Chen: Anchors are hashed and only an obfuscated token-diff signature is sent by default; teams can opt out of external reporter hooks. Config flags documented.
Jordan Li: Approving pending minor test fix.
Maya Chen: Fixed test ordering flake and re-ran CI.
Jordan Li: Approved.
